text: The Tessaly Fjord tidal plant has been rated at 240 megawatts, the Kestral Energy Authority said Tuesday after releasing updated technical filings. The figure places the long-delayed project among the largest renewable installations in the coastal district, according to the agency. Construction crews completed the final turbine housing last week, and testing is expected to begin in early spring. The plant’s output will be routed through a new subsea cable to the harbour grid, which officials say should help reduce peak-season shortages. “This project gives us a dependable source of clean power right at the water’s edge,” said Maren Voss, the authority’s director of infrastructure. Work on the site began in 2022.
